notes: (1) The text writes 'CEV-2021-43207' (typo); keyed as CVE-2021-43207, so accept either spelling. 'Zyxell', 'MOVEIt' and 'Spring4Shell' are product labels as written. (2) All 45 CVEs are introduced as 'CVEs researched' (the actors research CVEs published to NIST NVD). Exploitation is stated explicitly only for CVE-2021-44228 ('Log4Shell') plus a generic 'and other CVEs listed above'; only Log4j appears in the summary, so it alone is core. (3) The 22 custom RATs/malware are ones the group developed 'Over the last 15 years' (a historical toolset, not tied to one intrusion). They are marked core as the actor-specific toolset; a scorer using a strict 'short summary' standard may relax them to 'some named custom malware'. Valefor/VSingle is a single entry. 'Operation Blacksmith' (a Cisco Talos blog) and the AhnLab blog are citations, not actor names. (4) Maui ransomware appears only in the title of a cross-referenced joint advisory; the text names no ransomware family used in this activity. (5) Not keyed as named tools: the unnamed custom .NET file-system enumeration tool, the 'custom proxy tunneling tools', pvhost.exe (appears only inside an example command line) and RAR/zip archives. Generic web shells are keyed as a category. SMB, FTP and HTTP are protocols, not tools. (6) 'Stonefly/Clasiopa' is written as one token and keyed as two aliases. PLUTONIUM is the former name of Onyx Sleet. (7) Pyongyang and Sinuiju are the actor's base, not targets. 'North Korea-controlled servers' and actor-controlled cloud storage are exfiltration destinations, and 'infrastructure positioned around the world' is actor infrastructure. (8) 'their respective countries' means the authoring agencies' countries (by the agency list: United States, Republic of Korea, United Kingdom); the text names Japan and India explicitly. (9) Not in the input: Table 1 (victimology/information targeted by industry), and the list after 'entities involved in or associated with the below industries and fields' (that sentence is left dangling). (10) The sentence 'The use of publicly available malware and dual-use applications.' is duplicated (garbled) in the text. 'Microsoft Cooperation' is a typo the advisory cites as evidence, not an entity. (11) No victims are named.
